name: Energy Footprint Benchmark for Strong Parallel Electrified Powertrain
description: This work presents comprehensive energy management and in-depth energy footprint analysis of an electrified strong parallel commercial vehicle. We use the PS3 framework, validated real-world powertrain system models, and Pareto-optimal analysis to optimize fuel consumption and harmful pollutant emissions. The approach involves dynamic optimization of 13 states and 4 control levers with complex interactions between multiple subsystems for a parallel hybrid electric pick-up and delivery truck. These subsystems exhibit thermal, electrical, and mechanical dynamics at different time scales, and contain kinematic and combinatorial constraints, integer- and real-valued variables, interpolated look-up tables, and data maps. A Pareto-optimal solution is found by carefully optimizing fuel and NOx emissions to understand the energy footprint of the electrified powertrain. The presented results exhibit rich analysis and complex interactions among the powertrain subsystems to unearth a 7% improvement in its fuel consumption and 29% pollutant NOx reduction when compared to solution from a coarsely modeled powertrain system.
evaluation_method: multi-objective optimization (Pareto frontier) reported as percent reductions and trade-offs between fuel consumption and NOx emissions
general_score_metric: percent fuel consumption reduction and percent NOx emissions reduction (Pareto-frontier metrics)
typical_sota_score: 7% fuel consumption improvement and 29% NOx reduction (paper-reported improvement versus a coarse model); broader SOTA unknown
reputation: Niche academic benchmark in electrified powertrain and energy-management research with limited adoption outside specialized automotive/energy groups.
notes: Non-LLM, simulation-based benchmark using complex multi-physics dynamic models and bespoke validation; small/narrow domain (single vehicle type and drive cycles) and multi-objective metrics make cross-method comparisons nontrivial.
